name: Kinloch School
district_operator: Kinloch School District (until Feb 1, 1975); Ferguson-Florissant School District thereafter
notes: PROBABLE IDENTITY RESOLVED: the seed's generic 'Kinloch School' with closed=1975 almost certainly refers to Paul Laurence Dunbar Elementary, the first school for Black children in Kinloch — the only Kinloch school that closed in 1975. St. Louis REALTORS and the St. Louis Black Heritage Network date its opening to 1913; the State Historical Society of Missouri's Kinloch Photograph Collection finding aid (S0638) gives 1914-1975, so the open year is kept at 'probable' pending a primary source. Dunbar 'holds the record as the longest-operated school for blacks only' (Wikipedia/Kinloch, citing Kinloch histories). Closing mechanism is confirmed: in United States v. State of Missouri, 388 F. Supp. 1058 (E.D. Mo. 1975), the federal court ordered the Kinloch School District annexed to the Ferguson Reorganized School District R-2 (Ferguson-Florissant), effective February 1, 1975 — affirmed at 515 F.2d 1365 (8th Cir. 1975). Successor is therefore the Ferguson-Florissant School District at the district level (no matching school_id in dataset; its own rows appear in other batches). Other Kinloch schools for context, not this row: Vernon School (1927-1967) and Kinloch High School (opened 1936; separate rows ALL-393/ALL-497 in the dataset).

name: St. John the Baptist School
historical_names: St. John the Baptist Catholic School
St. John the Baptist Elementary School
notes: SURPRISE / LIKELY SEED LOCATION ERROR: no 'St. John the Baptist' parish or school is documented anywhere in the Kinloch/Florissant (north St. Louis County) area. The only Archdiocese of St. Louis school by this exact name is St. John the Baptist School at 5021 Adkins Ave, St. Louis 63116 (Bevo Mill, south city): parish organized Dec 30, 1913; elementary school opened September 1914 (parish history site); parish high school 1922-2008; grade school closed May 2014 (parish history, St. Louis Magazine, Post-Dispatch coverage). Values above describe that documented school. Alternative referents: (a) St. John the Baptist 'Gildehaus' School, Villa Ridge MO 63089, founded 1839, still open but far outside St. Louis County; (b) the actual Kinloch Catholic school the seed may have intended was Our Lady of the Angels Elementary (Holy Angels/Our Lady of the Angels Parish, 8122 Scott St., Kinloch, 1931-2002 per the St. Louis Genealogical Society closed-churches list — a separate real school that may merit its own row). Successor unknown: students dispersed to neighboring south-city parish schools.

name: Special School District of St. Louis County
historical_names: Special School District of St. Louis County
district_operator: Special School District of St. Louis County (SSD)
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT — multi-school countywide district, not a single yearbook-producing building. Per SSD's own 'Our Story' page: formed December 1957 by voter referendum creating a countywide special-education district with its own tax levy; began educating students 1958; opened its first dedicated school, Ackerman School (Florissant), in 1961; added career/technical education in the mid-1960s. Member/yearbook-producing schools (per SSD enrollment docs and Wikipedia): Ackerman School (Florissant), Litzsinger School (Ladue), Neuwoehner High School (Town and Country), Northview High School (Florissant), Southview School (Sunset Hills, elementary + HS programs), North Technical High School (Florissant), South Technical High School (Sunset Hills). Track B should redirect to these member schools, not this row. District remains operating.

name: Lambert-St. Louis International Airport Schools
district_operator: St. Louis County / Lambert Airport (per seed)
notes: LIKELY PHANTOM / UNRESOLVED LEAD: found no evidence any conventional school named 'Lambert Airport School' or on-airport school facility ever existed. The airfield began as Kinloch Airfield (leased by Albert Bond Lambert 1920, sold to the City of St. Louis 1928) per the City of St. Louis airport centennial page and flystl.com history; no school appears in the airport's documented history. Searched for schools serving airport employees' children and military-family schooling at Lambert — nothing found. The seed itself flags this as a research lead, not a confirmed school. Real entities it may be gesturing at: the Kinloch Park/Kinloch schools adjoining the airfield (Dunbar Elementary — see ALL-510 — Vernon School, Kinloch High School) and the Berkeley School District, whose residential tax base was repeatedly taken for runway expansion. Recommend collapsing this lead into ALL-549's airport-community placeholder rather than treating it as a school.

name: Saint Louis University
notes: Seed's 1818 confirmed by SLU's official timeline: Saint Louis Academy (later Saint Louis College) founded November 1818 at Bishop Louis DuBourg's request — first institution of higher learning west of the Mississippi; state charter as Saint Louis University granted 1832; Jesuits assumed operation 1826. Currently operating. Note: actual campus ZIP is 63103/63108 (midtown St. Louis city); seed's 63145 reflects 'served community' inclusion, not location.

name: Washington University in St. Louis
notes: Seed's 1853 confirmed by the university's own history page: charter for 'Eliot Seminary' drafted by State Sen. Wayman Crow and signed into law February 22, 1853; renamed to remove sectarian implication; inauguration ceremonies held April 22, 1857 (WashU Libraries). Currently operating. Actual campus ZIP is 63130 (Danforth Campus); seed's 63145 reflects 'served community' inclusion.

name: Lindenwood University
notes: SURPRISE / SEED DATE SUPERSEDED: seed lists 1827, the traditional founding year used since the 1920s (Reminiscences of Lindenwood College, 1920). Lindenwood's Board of Trustees unanimously adopted 1832 in February 2023 after primary-source review (Sibley correspondence and Mary Sibley's 1833 diary entry: 'I started the school in 1832'; the Sibleys did not reach St. Charles until May 1828). The university completed its official transition to 1832 branding by July 1, 2024. Recorded here at the corrected 1832. Located in St. Charles MO 63301 — well outside the RECA ZIP set; included by 'served community' only. Currently operating.

name: St. Louis County School Districts - Airport Area
notes: NOT A SCHOOL — the seed itself instructs 'Do not treat this as a school. Placeholder for boundary research.' Classified administrative_district_only so Track B skips it. The boundary churn the seed references is real: Lambert expansion and FAA noise-abatement buyouts repeatedly took residential land from the Kinloch, Berkeley, Pattonville, Hazelwood, and Ferguson-Florissant districts, and the 1975 federal desegregation order (388 F. Supp. 1058) redrew boundaries by annexing Kinloch SD and Berkeley SD into Ferguson-Florissant R-2 effective February 1, 1975. Any research this row was meant to trigger should be routed to the individual schools of those districts.

name: Lambert Airport Residential Community Schools
notes: NOT A SCHOOL — placeholder per seed notes ('Placeholder for schools whose historical addresses disappeared or whose attendance boundaries changed after airport expansion'). Classified administrative_district_only so Track B skips it and redirects to member schools. Schools/entities this placeholder most plausibly covers, from the documented Lambert-adjacent communities (Kinloch, Berkeley, Bridgeton, Robertson, Edmundson, Woodson Terrace): Dunbar Elementary (ALL-510, 1913-1975), Vernon School (Kinloch, 1927-1967), Kinloch High School (opened 1936 — ALL-393/ALL-497 elsewhere in dataset), Our Lady of the Angels Elementary (Kinloch, 1931-2002), Berkeley High School (closed 2004, replaced by McCluer South-Berkeley HS), and Pattonville R-3 schools lost to runway buyouts in Bridgeton. Ritenour also serves Edmundson/Woodson Terrace. Recommend a human dedupe pass mapping this placeholder to concrete rows.

name: Francis Howell High School
notes: Seed's 1881 confirmed via the district's official history: Francis Howell Institute opened September 12, 1881 in Howell's Prairie; Consolidated School District No. 2 of St. Charles County organized May 8, 1915; the renamed Francis Howell High School — 'a continuation of Francis Howell Institute' — held its first day September 6, 1915 (dedicated Feb 15, 1916 per Wikipedia). Recorded as a continuous 1881 lineage per the district's own framing. Remained the district's only high school until Francis Howell North opened 1986 (fhctoday.com). Yearbook: Howelltonian. Currently operating at 7001 Hwy 94 S.

name: Francis Howell Central High School
notes: SURPRISE / SEED DATE CORRECTED: seed lists 1987; actual opening day was August 21, 1997 — confirmed by FHC's own student-publication anniversary issue and the district's About-page timeline ('Francis Howell Central ... open (1997)'). It was the district's third high school, after FHHS (1881) and Francis Howell North (1986); opened with only freshmen and sophomores (Classes of 2000 and 2001). Located at 5199 Hwy N, Cottleville (mailing address St. Charles 63304). Currently operating.
